    The cycle of a closed walk with a sink and the functor L #

    Setting 3.11 and Construction 3.12, in the dual form with a sink. A primitive cyclically reduced closed walk w of length r = n + 2 whose cycle D_w is not oriented has a sink u. The cycle is recorded with u as none and the other n + 1 vertices some 0, …, some n in cyclic order; the two arrows into u come from some 0 (first) and some n (second), and the n middle arrows join some j and some (j + 1) with an orientation ε j (true: towards some (j + 1)).

    For a Kronecker module T = (V, W; a, b), L(T) has W at u, V at the other vertices, a and b on the first and second arrows into u, and identities on the middle arrows. This is the construction of the paper applied to the opposite walk followed by the duality; with a sink, L(S₋) is the simple representation at u.
